mainTopic: Exact precision (אפשר לצמצם) in עגלה ערופה, and two male firstborn lambs born together: who gets which, and whether the second owes מתנות.
overview: The amud opens by explaining that the earlier opinion follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that exact precision (אפשר לצמצם) is possible. The גמרא then looks at a ברייתא about a body found exactly between two towns (עגלה ערופה). It concludes that the תנאים there argue about the word קרובה, not about precision. Another ברייתא, where the חכמים say the towns share one calf with a condition, proves that the רבנן hold exact precision is impossible, even for things in human hands. The גמרא then returns to the משנה of two male lambs whose heads came out together. רבי טרפון gives the כהן the better lamb, because the healthier one probably came out first. רבי יוחנן explains that according to רבי עקיבא the כהן takes the leaner one, and proves this from the end of the משנה. Next comes the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about whether the second lamb owes מתנות, each with its reason. רבי אלעזר limits that מחלוקת to cases where the כהן already holds a replacement. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a challenge from רבי יוסי's words, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He follows רבי יוסי הגלילי: precision is possible
steps.stepSummary: The opinion just discussed holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי, that exact precision is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: He agrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said: It is possible for things in Heaven's hands to line up exactly, and all the more so for things in human hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the discussion that came just before this point. It says the sage being discussed holds like רבי יוסי הגלילי, who believes exact precision can happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If things done by Heaven, like two births at the exact same moment, can line up perfectly, then things people measure can line up perfectly too. This means his view is a separate opinion. You cannot use it to learn what the חכמים hold.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to be exactly precise, so two things can match perfectly
In the hands of Heaven, meaning things that happen naturally
In human hands, meaning things people do or measure

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
phrases.notes: "He" is the sage mentioned just before this point, רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: who said: it is possible to be exactly precise in Heaven's hands,
and all the more so in human hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the discussion that came just before this text by tying the opinion to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the view to a different tannaitic opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have used this opinion to learn the view of the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: This opinion follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds precision is possible, so it tells us nothing about the חכמים.

steps.title: Suggestion: the תנאים of עגלה ערופה argue about precision
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that a ברייתא about a body found exactly between two towns is an argument over whether precision is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is an argument between תנאים? If a body was found exactly between two towns, they would not break the calf's neck at all. רבי אליעזר says: both towns bring two calves. Isn't the argument this: the תנא קמא holds precision is impossible, and רבי אליעזר holds precision is possible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about עגלה ערופה. It suggests that the two sides there are arguing over whether exact precision is possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says no calf is brought, and the suggestion is that this is because he thinks one town must really be closer. רבי אליעזר says each town brings a calf, and the suggestion is that this is because he thinks a perfect tie is real.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this is an argument between תנאים?
Breaking the neck of the עגלה ערופה
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
Is it not so that…? (a way of proposing an explanation)

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like an argument of the Tannaim:
If a slain body was found exactly between two towns —
they would not break the calf's neck,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
the two of them bring two calves.
Is it not that they argue about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם,
phrases.english: that the first Tanna holds it is impossible to be exactly precise,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds it is possible to be exactly precise?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for an argument between תנאים over the precision question that came up in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the עגלה ערופה argument really about whether precision is possible?

steps.title: Rejection: they could share one calf with a condition
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא קמא held precision is impossible, the towns could bring one shared calf with a condition, so that cannot be his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think so? If the תנא קמא holds precision is impossible, why would they not break a calf's neck at all? Let them bring one calf as partners and make a condition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one town must really be closer, then a calf is owed, but we just don't know which town owes it. The simple fix would be for both towns to share one calf and say it belongs to whichever town is truly closer. Since the תנא קמא says no calf at all, his reason cannot be that precision is impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think that? (a way of pushing back)
And let them make a condition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תנא קמא lets them skip the calf because no town is closer. The point is that if one town really were closer, a shared calf with a condition would solve the problem.

phrases.english: And can you think so?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם,
phrases.english: If the first Tanna holds it is impossible to be exactly precise,
why would they not break the calf's neck?
Let them bring one calf in partnership and make a condition!
phrases.notes: The condition would be that the calf counts for whichever town is really the closer one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא proposed in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: How the proposal reads the תנא קמא's opinion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If precision were impossible, a shared calf with a condition would work, so the תנא קמא's ruling of no calf does not fit that reason.

steps.title: Real argument: does 'nearest' allow more than one town?
steps.stepSummary: All agree precision is possible; they argue whether the word קרובה limits the obligation to one single town.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for these תנאים everyone agrees precision is possible. Here they argue about 'קרובה' and not 'קרובות.' The תנא קמא holds: 'nearest' in the singular, so not several nearest towns. רבי אליעזר holds: 'nearest,' and even several nearest towns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the ברייתא. The argument is about how to read one word in the פסוק, not about precision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides accept that a perfect tie can happen. The תנא קמא reads the singular word קרובה as meaning only one town brings a calf, so a tie means no calf at all. רבי אליעזר says the word also covers two towns that are equally nearest, so each town brings a calf.

keyTerms.meaning: Nearest (singular), the word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The עגלה ערופה argument is not about whether precision is possible, since everyone agrees it is. It is about whether the פסוק's word קרובה limits the obligation to one town.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the ברייתא as a source for an argument over precision. The question of אפשר לצמצם must be decided from other sources.

phrases.english: Rather, according to these Tannaim,
everyone agrees it is possible to be exactly precise,
and here they argue about "nearest" and not several nearest,
that the first Tanna holds: "nearest," and not several nearest,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds: "nearest," and even several nearest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 rejected the precision explanation, this gives a new reason for the argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the argument from logic to how the פסוק is read
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue over whether exact precision is possible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree precision is possible. They argue whether קרובה means only one town or can include several towns that are equally nearest.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא of the body between two towns is an argument about reading the פסוק, not about אפשר לצמצם.

steps.title: What is the final conclusion about the Rabbis' view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final conclusion is regarding the רבנן's view on whether exact precision is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about it?
steps.whatsHappening: After the back-and-forth about precision, the גמרא asks what the final answer is about the רבנן's opinion. This is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 left the ברייתא open, since both sides could hold precision is possible. The גמרא now wants a firm answer about what the רבנן hold, especially for things done by people.

keyTerms.meaning: What was concluded about it? (asking for the final answer)
To be exactly precise (for two things to be exactly equal or happen at the exact same moment)

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?
phrases.notes: "It" means the question of whether the רבנן think exact precision is possible, even for things people do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the previous attempt to settle the matter was pushed off, the גמרא asks for a final conclusion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the רבנן hold that exact precision is possible or impossible, even for things done by human hands?

steps.title: A ברייתא about a body found exactly between two towns
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין, quoting רב עמרם, brings a ברייתא: if a body is found exactly between two towns, רבי אליעזר says both bring two calves, and the חכמים say they bring one shared calf with a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב עמרם: A ברייתא teaches that if the body was found exactly between two towns, רבי אליעזר says the two towns bring two calves. The חכמים say they bring one calf together as partners and make a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer the question. Here it only quotes the ברייתא; the next step will analyze it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is the חכמים's ruling: one calf, bought together, with a condition. The condition is that the calf counts for whichever town is really closer. This unusual ruling will be the key to the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly in the middle, precisely equal distance
The calf (עגלה ערופה) brought by the town closest to a murdered body

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin said
that Rav Amram said:

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא נִמְצָא מְכוָּּון בֵּין שְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת,
phrases.english: It was taught: If [the body] was found exactly between two towns,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
The two of them bring two calves,
And the Sages say:
They bring one calf in partnership and make a condition.
phrases.notes: The condition is that the calf belongs to whichever town is truly closer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם: תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by bringing a ברייתא that will be analyzed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא where the חכמים rule that the two towns bring one shared calf with a condition.

steps.title: Neither 'possible' option fits the Rabbis' ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that if the רבנן held precision is possible, their ruling of one shared calf makes no sense under either reading of the word קרובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do the רבנן hold? If they hold that exact precision is possible, and the word 'closest' includes even several closest towns, then they should bring two calves! And if 'closest' means only one town and not several, then they should not bring even one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the חכמים's ruling against the idea that precision is possible. It shows that this idea leads to either two calves or no calf, never one shared calf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the towns could really be exactly equal, there are only two options. If קרובה includes two towns, each must bring a calf. If קרובה means only one town, then neither town is obligated. One shared calf fits neither option.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The closest [town]', the word in the פסוק about עגלה ערופה (singular)

phrases.english: What do the Rabbis hold?
If the Rabbis hold that exact precision is possible,
and 'closest' includes even several closest [towns],
phrases.notes: This is the word from the פסוק, דברים 21:3.

phrases.english: then let them bring two [calves]!
And if 'closest' means one, and not several closest [towns],
then they should not bring even one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן? אִי קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן דְּאֶפְשָׁר לְצַמְצֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from step 6, using the two readings of קרובה from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן hold exact precision is impossible.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים's ruling in the ברייתא of one shared calf with a condition, which cannot fit the view that precision is possible.

steps.title: The Rabbis hold precision is impossible, even for human actions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the רבנן hold exact precision is impossible, even for things done by people, and accepts this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that the רבנן hold exact precision is impossible, even for things done by people? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the previous step and confirms it with שמע מינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared calf with a condition only makes sense if one town must really be closer, even though we cannot tell which. So the רבנן hold that two things can never be exactly equal. Measuring the distance between towns is something people do, so this applies even to things in human hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, do we not learn from this...?
By human hands, things people do
Learn from it (the conclusion is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, exact precision is impossible, and this is true even for things done by people. That is why the two towns bring one calf with a condition: one of them must truly be closer.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קָסָבְרִי רַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this that the Rabbis hold:
exact precision is impossible,
and even [for things done] by human hands.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that the proof in step 7 was building toward.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The רבנן hold that exact precision is impossible, even for things done by human hands.

steps.title: Why does רבי טרפון let the כהן choose the better lamb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי טרפון from the משנה, that the כהן chooses the better of the two lambs, and asks for his reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: The כהן chooses the better one for himself. What is רבי טרפון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next opinion in the משנה about two male lambs whose heads came out together. It asks why רבי טרפון gives the כהן the better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we do not know which lamb came out first, why should the כהן get the better one? The גמרא wants the reason behind this choice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says:
phrases.notes: Back to our משנה: two male lambs born to a first-time mother, and their heads came out together.

phrases.english: [The priest] chooses the better one for himself.
What is Rabbi Tarfon's reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר: בּוֹרֵר לוֹ אֶת הַיָּפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the precision discussion to the next opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רבי טרפון's ruling that the כהן takes the better lamb.

steps.title: The healthier lamb came out first
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון holds that the healthier lamb probably came out first, so it is the firstborn and belongs to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the healthier one comes out first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי טרפון assumes the stronger, healthier lamb was born first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the true firstborn goes to the כהן. רבי טרפון assumes the healthier lamb pushed out first, so he treats it as the firstborn. That is why the כהן takes the better one.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָבַר: הָהוּא דְּבָרִיא נָפֵק בְּרֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: He holds: The one that is healthier comes out first.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבַר: הָהוּא דְּבָרִיא נָפֵק בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The healthier lamb is assumed to have come out first, so it is the firstborn.

steps.title: According to רבי עקיבא, the כהן takes the leaner lamb
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: according to רבי עקיבא's view in the משנה (משמנין), the כהן takes the leaner lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'They assess...' etc. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The כהן takes the leaner one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's view from the משנה, and רבי יוחנן explains what it means in practice: the כהן gets the thinner lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's words משמנין ביניהן could sound like the two sides split the value. רבי יוחנן says that is not the meaning; the כהן simply takes the leaner lamb. This explanation sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They assess the value (literally, 'they fatten'); the opening word of רבי עקיבא's view
Etc.: the rest of the quote is in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: 'They assess...' etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה is 'they assess between them' (משמנין ביניהן).

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The priest takes the lean one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next opinion in the משנה, רבי עקיבא's, after finishing רבי טרפון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the כהן takes the leaner of the two lambs.

steps.title: Doesn't the משנה say they split the value?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא challenges רבי יוחנן: the משנה says משמנין ביניהן, which sounds like the two sides share the value, not that the כהן takes the lean one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to רבי יוחנן: But we learned in the משנה, 'they assess between them'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא pushes back against רבי יוחנן's explanation, using the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'they assess between them' sounds like the value is divided between the כהן and the owner. That seems to contradict the idea that the כהן simply takes the leaner lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it that...? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Yochanan:
But we learned: 'They assess between them'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's statement in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the כהן takes the lean lamb.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'assess between them' suggest the value is divided between the two sides, not that the כהן takes one specific lamb.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן learned it from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that while רבי חייא בר אבא was still in בבל, he had already explained this from the later part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: While you were still eating dates in בבל, we already explained it from the later part of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends his explanation. He says the later part of the משנה shows that the כהן takes the lean lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not read the opening words by themselves. He reads them together with the end of the משנה, which explains how things actually work out, and that shows the כהן takes the leaner lamb. The remark about dates in בבל is a friendly jab: 'we worked this out long before you got here.'

keyTerms.meaning: Dates (especially unripe ones), a common food in בבל
From the later part (of the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'eating dates in בבל' as part of the law. It is just a way of saying 'long before you came here, we already solved this.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד דַּאֲכַלְתְּ כַּפְנְיָיתָא בְּבָבֶל,
phrases.english: He said to him: While you were eating dates in Babylonia,
phrases.notes: Basically: 'While you were still back home in בבל, we already figured this out here in ארץ ישראל.'

phrases.english: we explained it from the latter clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד דַּאֲכַלְתְּ כַּפְנְיָיתָא בְּבָבֶל, תַּרְגֵּימְנָא מִסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the opening words in light of the later part of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משמנין ביניהן means the כהן and the owner split the value.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later part of the משנה shows the opening words do not mean splitting the value; the כהן takes the leaner lamb.

steps.title: Proof from the later part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings his proof from the סיפא. When one lamb died, רבי עקיבא does not split the remaining one. So משמנין in the רישא cannot mean splitting either.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the later part of the משנה teaches: if one of the lambs died, רבי טרפון says they divide the remaining one, and רבי עקיבא says the one who wants to take from his fellow must bring proof. Now if you think 'משמנין בניהן' means they split the value, then here too רבי עקיבא should have them split!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן shows the proof he had mentioned in Step 13. It comes from the סיפא of the משנה, where one lamb died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, רבי עקיבא rules that the owner keeps the lamb unless the כהן brings proof. He does not split it. If רבי עקיבא really meant 'split' in the רישא, he should rule the same way in the סיפא, and he doesn't.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה
Whoever wants to take something from another person must bring the proof
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: As the later part teaches:
If one of them died,
Rabbi Tarfon says: They divide it,
Rabbi Akiva says:
The one who takes from his fellow must bring the proof.
phrases.notes: So the lamb stays with the owner unless the כהן can prove it is the בכור.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that 'they assess between them' means they split it with each other,
then here too, let them split it with each other!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, ליפלגי; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets, ליפלוג.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the proof from the סיפא that רבי יוחנן said he had already given in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that, according to רבי עקיבא, the כהן takes the leaner lamb
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: when one lamb died, רבי עקיבא rules המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה instead of splitting.

steps.title: משמנין means the extra fat is in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads משמנין as coming from שומן (fat). The extra fat of the better lamb is in doubt between them, so the owner tells the כהן to bring proof if he wants it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'משמנין' mean? The fat is in question between them. The owner says to the כהן: bring proof that this one is the בכור, and then take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of משמנין. This answers רבי חייא בר אבא's challenge from Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משמנין does not mean 'they share the value.' It means the extra fat of the better lamb is the thing in doubt. Since the owner can say 'prove it,' the כהן ends up with the leaner lamb, just as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: From the word שׁוֹמֶן (fat). Here it refers to the extra fat that is in doubt
Fat (the extra value of the healthier lamb)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, the owner keeps the better lamb and the כהן gets the leaner one. The כהן can take the better one only if he brings proof that it is the בכור.

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'they assess' mean?
The fat will be in question between them,
phrases.notes: This is a play on words: משמנין sounds like שומן. The better lamb's extra fat is what they disagree over.

phrases.english: for the owner says to the priest:
Bring proof that it is the firstborn, and take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in Step 14 and gives the new reading of משמנין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משמנין means the כהן and the owner split the value between them.
steps.terutzMaskana: משמנין means the extra fat is in doubt, so the כהן must bring proof to take the better lamb. Without proof he gets the leaner one.

steps.title: Why must the owner give מתנות from the second lamb?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the second lamb grazes until it gets a blemish and owes מתנות, while רבי יוסי exempts it. Then it asks for רבי מאיר's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the second lamb must graze until it becomes blemished, and it owes the priestly gifts, but רבי יוסי exempts it. What is the reasoning of רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about the second lamb that stays with the owner. It asks why רבי מאיר says the owner must give מתנות from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second lamb might be the בכור, so it cannot be eaten until it has a blemish. The question is whether it also owes the regular gifts (זרוע, לחיים, קיבה) that any ordinary animal owes.

keyTerms.meaning: It grazes until it gets a blemish
The priestly gifts (foreleg, jaw, and maw) taken from an ordinary slaughtered animal

phrases.english: And the second must graze until it becomes blemished,
and it is obligated in the gifts,
and Rabbi Yosei exempts it.
What is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir?
phrases.notes: The unnamed first opinion in the משנה belongs to רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה: the מתנות owed from the second lamb.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the first opinion (רבי מאיר) requires מתנות from the second lamb

steps.title: The כהן has a claim either way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the כהן wins either way. If the lamb is the בכור, all of it is his. If not, he gets the מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Since the כהן comes at him from two sides. He says to the owner: if it is the בכור, all of it is mine. If it is not the בכור, give me the gifts from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question from Step 16. He explains why רבי מאיר makes the owner give מתנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, in a doubt, the owner keeps what is in his hands. Here the כהן has a claim no matter which way the doubt turns out, so the owner cannot avoid giving at least the מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: From two sides (two claims that each cover the other)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְכֹהֵן בָּא עָלָיו מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין,
phrases.english: Since the priest comes at him from two sides,
for he says to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּכוֹר הוּא — כּוּלֵּיהּ דִּידִי הוּא,
phrases.english: If it is the firstborn, all of it is mine;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא בְּכוֹר הוּא — הַב לִי מַתָּנוֹת מִינֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: if it is not the firstborn, give me the gifts from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוֹאִיל וְכֹהֵן בָּא עָלָיו מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן has a claim either way: the whole animal if it is the בכור, or the מתנות if it is not. So the owner must give the מתנות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'two sides' reasoning lets the כהן collect something even though the case is a doubt.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי exempts the second lamb from מתנות, given רבי יוחנן's strong 'two sides' argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reasoning of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the other side of the מחלוקת. It wants to know why רבי יוסי says the owner owes no מתנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After Step 17, it seems the כהן clearly deserves something either way. So the גמרא needs to explain how רבי יוסי answers that argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who exempts the second lamb from מתנות
Firstborn male animal, which belongs to the כהן

phrases.english: And what is the reasoning of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason of the other opinion in the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוסי exempts the second lamb from מתנות

steps.title: As if the כהן took it and sold it back
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the חכמים treated the כהן as if he had acquired the second lamb and then sold it back to the owner with its blemish. So the owner owes no gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They treated one who did not acquire as one who acquired. Even though the lamb never reached the כהן's hands, it is as if it reached his hands and he sold it to the ישראל with its blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 18 and gives רבי יוסי's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן already received one lamb. So the second lamb is viewed as if it went to the כהן and was sold back to the owner as a blemished animal. Because of this, the owner can claim it is not an ordinary animal that owes מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) made it, treated it as

phrases.english: Rava said:
They treated one who does not acquire as one who acquires,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן, who never actually got this second lamb.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְטָא לִידֵיהּ
phrases.english: and even though it did not reach his hands,
it is as if it reached his hands,
and he sold it to the Israelite with its blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא עָשׂוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה כְּזוֹכֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second lamb is treated as if the כהן acquired it and sold it back blemished, so the owner is exempt from מתנות.

steps.title: Everyone agrees when the כהן got nothing in exchange
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר limits the מחלוקת. When the כהן received no replacement animal, everyone, even רבי יוסי, agrees that the ספק בכור owes מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Everyone agrees about a ספק בכור where the כהן has no replacement in his hand, that it owes the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds a new statement. It shows where the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's exemption depends on the idea that the כהן already got one lamb in its place (Step 19). If the כהן got nothing, there is nothing to treat as an exchange. So everyone agrees the owner gives the מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that may or may not be a בכור
A replacement, something received in its place

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי exempts the second lamb only because the כהן already received a lamb in exchange. With no exchange, everyone agrees that מתנות are owed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Everyone agrees about an uncertain firstborn
where there is no replacement in the priest's hand,
that it is obligated in the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בִּסְפֵק בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of the מחלוקת explained in Steps 17 and 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the כהן holds no replacement animal, a ספק בכור owes מתנות according to everyone.

steps.title: Isn't רבי אלעזר's statement obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who 'everyone agrees' is meant to include. If it means רבי יוסי, that seems obvious. His exemption rests on the idea that the כהן already holds a replacement, so with no replacement his reason does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone agrees.' Who is he talking about? רבי יוסי? That's obvious! רבי יוסי only exempts the owner there, where the כהן holds a replacement animal. In that case the חכמים treated the כהן, who did not really acquire the lamb, as if he had acquired it. But when the כהן holds no replacement, רבי יוסי would not exempt the owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר from Step 20. It says his point that 'everyone, even רבי יוסי, agrees' seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19, רבא explained רבי יוסי's exemption this way: the כהן was treated as if he had acquired the second lamb and sold it back. That idea only works when the כהן already holds a replacement animal. So when there is no replacement, of course רבי יוסי would make the owner give the מתנות. Why did רבי אלעזר need to tell us?

keyTerms.meaning: A replacement or exchange: here, the animal the כהן already received
Treating someone who did not acquire as if he did acquire

phrases.english: 'Everyone agrees': who is meant?
phrases.notes: These are רבי אלעזר's words from the step just before this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei? That's obvious!

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא פָטַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only exempts there,
where a replacement is in the priest's hand,
since they treated one who did not acquire like one who acquired,
phrases.notes: This is רבא's explanation from Step 19: the כהן is treated as if he took the lamb and sold it back.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן — לָא!
phrases.english: but where no replacement is in the priest's hand — no!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים מַאן? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי? פְּשִׁיטָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי אלעזר's statement in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that everyone agrees when there is no replacement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's reason for רבי יוסי depends on the כהן holding a replacement. So the case with no replacement obviously requires מתנות, and the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought רבי יוסי had a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The statement is needed after all. We might have thought רבי יוסי exempts the owner so he won't come to shear or work the animal. That worry would apply even with no replacement, so רבי אלעזר teaches us that this is not the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי יוסי's reason is this: if you make the owner give מתנות, he will come to shear the animal and work with it. Then he would be exempt even when the כהן holds no replacement. So רבי אלעזר comes to teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'it's obvious' challenge. It shows a different reason someone could have given for רבי יוסי, one that would have made his exemption much wider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner has to give מתנות, he might think the animal is plain חולין. Then he might shear it or make it work, which is forbidden for a possible בכור. If that were רבי יוסי's reason, he would exempt the owner even with no replacement. רבי אלעזר's statement rules this out: רבי יוסי's reason must be the 'treated as acquired' idea, which needs a replacement.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea)

steps.confusionAlert: Being obligated in מתנות does not make this animal plain חולין. The worry is only that the owner might mistakenly treat it that way and shear or work it.

phrases.english: You might have said:
the reason of Rabbi Yosei is that he holds
that if you obligate him in the gifts —
he will come to shearing and working it,
phrases.notes: He might think the animal is plain חולין, though shearing or working a possible בכור is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין חֲלִיפִין בְּיַד כֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: so he would be exempt even though there is no replacement in the priest's hand,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of Step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a possible mistaken reading (מהו דתימא) that makes the statement needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי exempts because of the worry about shearing and work, even with no replacement
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי's exemption depends on the replacement, so with no replacement everyone agrees the owner owes מתנות
steps.whyThisMatters: It pins down that רבי יוסי's reason is the 'treated as acquired' idea, not the worry about shearing and work.

steps.title: A challenge from the end of the משנה begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the מהו דתימא of Step 22. How could anyone have thought רבי יוסי's reason was the worry about shearing and work? The end of the משנה quotes רבי יוסי's own words, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say that? Doesn't the end of the משנה teach that רבי יוסי used to say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against Step 22. It opens a quote of רבי יוסי from the end of the משנה, and the content of the quote comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge asks whether the mistaken idea in Step 22 could ever have been held. The proof will come from רבי יוסי's own words in the end of the משנה, which show what his exemption depends on. Those words begin on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the משנה

phrases.english: And can you really say this?
But doesn't the end of the Mishnah teach,
that Rabbi Yosei used to say:
phrases.notes: The quote itself continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The מהו דתימא of Step 22, that one might have thought רבי יוסי's reason is the worry about shearing and work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's own words in the end of the משנה (quoted on the next amud) are brought to show that the mistaken idea in Step 22 could not have been held, so רבי אלעזר's statement would again seem unnecessary.
